facts.fact: 作者回忆读 Pierre Hadot 在《The Present Alone Is Our Happiness》中回答采访时曾感到失望，十五年后（Fifteen years later）自认当时对这位陷入 performative contradiction 的老人过苛；那道问题是 Arnold Davidson 所问：哲学话语与（非纯概念的）实践在 Hadot 自己的哲学观中扮演何种角色。
facts.anchor: Iremember feeling disappointed when I read Pierre Hadot’s reply to his interviewer

facts.fact: 作者把 Davidson 的问题读出四种可能的意涵，并选定第四种——要 Hadot 当场显现真正的哲学家；佐证之一是 Hadot 讲述他幼年遇见的未来的 John XXIII 因餐桌服务不当而 “furious”，并断言 “[I]n my eyes this man is not a saint”。
facts.anchor: Hadot relates an anecdote about the future John XXIII whom he met when he was a young boy

facts.fact: Hadot 自认 discourse/practices 之分借自 Stoics，作答中两度以 “Personally” 转折、明言要 “once again take a detour by way of antiquity”；作者以 Matthew 7:16（“by his fruits”）、Orwell（“At 50, everyone has the face he deserves”）与《Tao Te Ching》（“those who know do not speak”）为衡量 Hadot 的尺度。
facts.anchor: I borrowed this distinction [between discourse and practices] from the Stoics

facts.fact: Hadot 在自白中承认行史家与注释家之职时尽力过哲学生活但 “the results are not always of a very high level”，住院期间（sojourns in hospitals）未能保持想望的心之宁静，并引 Georges Friedmann “to take flight every day”，自认年岁渐长愈来愈 “prefer experience to discourse”。
facts.anchor: And during my sojourns in hospitals, for example, I have not always maintained the serenity of mind

facts.fact: 作者判 Davidson 的总结性回应（“Thus a priority of practice…”）为悲剧性的（tragic），指其无视 Hadot 的回应已暴露他未能超越自己温和批评的学院哲学，并称整场交流是一出喜剧、由此通向 religion as a way of life。
facts.anchor: While his summary is technically correct, he is blind to how Hadot's response has disclosed

facts.fact: 作者列举 philosophy as a way of life 的缺陷：在现代性中偏向 discourse 而非 life、滑向 self-help 与 “modern stoicism”、只有 a la carte 式灵修而无真正道路、无 epistemic verification、无可辨认的 Sage；对比之下禅宗由 recognized roshi 面谈学生以 discern satori（“clear seeing of self-nature”）。
facts.anchor: Whereas Zen Buddhism uses an interview process in which a recognized roshi interrogates a student

facts.fact: 2013 年 12 月（December 2013）作者的长姐 Jen 被送进医院，查出 “of indeterminate origin” 的癌症；一月初作者与她谈起她与丈夫在新居后院刚种下的果树；Twelve weeks later 她去世。姐姐意外死后作者起初转向禅宗（Zen Buddhism），并自陈直到 Jen 死于 2014 才质疑其追求善好生活的形而上学基础——此前他一直受 Charles Taylor 所谓 “the immanent frame”（《A Secular Age》）的束缚；注脚显示他曾在 First Things（March 2020）发表 “Secular Monks” 一文。
facts.anchor: In December 2013, my oldest sister Jen was taken to the hospital.

facts.fact: 2019 年 1 月（January 2019）在作者第二次参加的禅修营（sesshin）首日，Rinzai Zen teacher Jeff Shore 问他 “What brings you here?”，作者答 “Enlightenment—the longing to know who I am”；Shore 又问他的 natural koan，作者以 “Is this all there is? Is this it?” 作答，Shore 指示其继续 zazen with extended outbreath、静默参究 koan 到底。
facts.anchor: Jeff Shore, a Rinzai Zen teacher, asked me on the first day of the sesshin. It was January 2019
